literal: Than those who love sweet words without receiving, in the world, than those who live, hard-hearted people there is none.
translation: There are no people in this world more hard-hearted than those who continue to live even without receiving sweet words of comfort from their beloved.
modern: தங்களை விரும்புபவரிடமிருந்து இனிய சொற்களைப் பெறாமல், இந்த உலகத்தில் உயிர் வாழ்கின்றவர்களைப் போல வன்நெஞ்சம் உடையவர்கள் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: In this couplet, the pining heroine speaks of her own state of survival during separation. She laments that she is still alive despite not hearing any sweet, comforting words from her beloved. By calling those who survive such grief 'வன்கணார்' (hard-hearted or stubborn ones), she mockingly accuses herself of having an incredibly tough, unyielding heart that refuses to break and let her die, highlighting the sheer intensity of her solitary suffering.
